titulo.texto: Walk: Toward the Plaza of the Stela

frase_gancho.texto: A short stretch to listen to as you climb.

puente_narrativo.texto: You have reached the Plaza of the Stela of the Two Glyphs.

guion_corto.texto: Follow the signs toward the Plaza of the Stela of the Two Glyphs. As you walk, look at the terraces and stone walls around you. Kenneth Hirth tells us that people lived on large terraces and platforms on the hillsides, and that the houses spread toward the valley floor. Paved causeways connected the sectors of the city. They were not decoration: they carried people, goods, and news from one neighborhood to another. If the path climbs, think that whoever lived here climbed it every day. When you reach a wide plaza with a stela at its center, you are exactly where you were meant to be.

guion_largo.texto:
This is a walk. You do not need to stop. Follow the signs toward the Plaza of the Stela of the Two Glyphs and let the audio keep you company.

As you move forward, look at the terraces and stone walls around you. Kenneth Hirth explains that people lived on large terraces and platforms on the hillsides, and that the houses spread toward the valley floor. What you see as landscape was once a neighborhood.

Paved causeways connected the sectors of the city. They were not decoration. They carried people, goods, and news from one neighborhood to another.

If the path climbs, think that whoever lived here climbed it every day, with a load or without one. In a city of hills, walking was part of the work.

When you reach a wide plaza with a stela at its center, you are already at the next audio.

texto: Notice the walls that hold up the terraces
Look for how many directions the path has
Walk slowly and take in the landscape
